_comment: Igris-ai PROJECT harness manifest (FR-136). Declares the 9 core agents whose codex harnesses are mechanically regenerated from their canonical core/agents/<name>.md prompts (TD-021). Core ships only the SCHEMA (core/scripts/cli-adapters/manifest.schema.json); each project ships its own data manifest at its repo root. Canonical is the SOLE source of truth; every target listed here is a GENERATED artifact - editing a target file directly is a process error. Personal/Layer-2 customizations are NOT declared here - they live in an optional gitignored overlay at ~/.igris/loadout/harness-manifest.personal.json (FR-139). FR-202 M4: the os_identity surface (TD-233) was retired — the orchestrator no longer projects an identity region into any harness's auto-read file. The per-harness delegation mechanism is now a CONTEXT LAYER (core/os/harness-specific/<harness>.md, loaded at Boot for the Detect-resolved harness), not a projected surface.
_harnesses_comment: Per-harness `delegation_model` — the applicability predicate for the harness-specific context layer (FR-202 M4). `native-static` = the harness loads Igris agents statically and a skill delegating via `subagent_type:<agent>` resolves directly (no harness-specific file needed). `dynamic-define` = the harness cannot load static Igris agents but defines subagents at runtime (e.g. Antigravity `define_subagent`/`invoke_subagent`); it has a `core/os/harness-specific/<harness>.md` file pointing at the shared delegation recipe, so the orchestrator is taught 'read ~/.igris/core/agents/<X>.md → define_subagent → invoke' ONCE at Boot, with ZERO per-skill branching. A harness absent from this map defaults to native-static. This is no longer a projected surface (the recipe was re-homed off the identity region into the harness-specific layer); the map survives only to select which harness-specific file applies. FR-217: each harness block is EXTENDED into the canonical harness descriptor — `agent_id` (the npx agent id; differs only claude→claude-code, gemini→gemini-cli), `agents`{target_type,projection} (absent for antigravity = dynamic-define, no static agent surface), `mcp`{config_path,format,map_key,entry_shape} (antigravity rides the gemini entry_shape but a DISTINCT config_path, FR-179 R1), `grant`{kind,path?,token?}, `hooks`{supported,config_path?,method?}, and `harness_specific_file?`. This is the SINGLE source of truth every harness-wiring consumer reads (TS via cli/src/lib/harness-descriptor.ts). Per-surface participation is DERIVED from block presence (agents/mcp/hooks.supported/grant), not a separate list. TD-281: `mcp.projected` and `hooks.projected` are the per-surface 'surface-projected vs carve-out' flags the drift parity-guard reads — `true` = this harness's targets SHOULD appear in every surface block (so a block omitting it that a sibling declares is a PARITY anomaly); `false` = a deliberate carve-out (antigravity `mcp.projected:false` = the FR-179 custom-write to ~/.gemini/config/, NOT surface-projected via add-mcp). Projection CAPABILITY (block presence) and projection EXPECTATION (the projected flag) are now distinct: all 5 have an mcp block but only {claude,codex,gemini,opencode} are mcp-projected; the 3 supported-hook harnesses {claude,opencode,antigravity} are all hook-projected (no hook carve-out today). FR-192: cursor is the 6th harness — a single-agent harness with NO subagent spawning, so it carries the NEW `delegation_model:inline` (the orchestrator ADOPTS the target agent's prompt inline rather than delegating to a static or runtime-defined subagent; see core/os/harness-specific/_inline-delegation-recipe.md). cursor has NO `agents` block (no static-agent surface; cursor-agent has no subagent file mechanism) and `hooks.supported:false` (no hook API); its MCP rides the `claude` entry_shape into ~/.cursor/mcp.json (mcpServers + type:stdio — REUSE, no new emitter) and its grant is `covered` (cursor-agent auto-approves MCP at runtime via --approve-mcps; no persistent grant file, like opencode). Additive — still v1.
